newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland wants to join EU monetary, currency union.
newsitem.headline: Poland wants to join EU monetary, currency union.

text.p: Poland's President Aleksander Kwasniewski will this week declare his country's intention to join the European Union's planned monetary and currency union as soon as possible, his spokesman said on Tuesday.
Antoni Styrczula said Kwasniewski would outline Poland's drive for EU membership during a speech to the College of Europe in Natolin near Warsaw on Wednesday.
Kwasniewski will argue that, in the process of European integration, it is vital to foresee and anticipate future developments, Styrczula said in a statement.
"In the light of this, Poland is already now adopting as its goal entry into monetary and currency union as fast as possible, and joining the hard core of integration," the advance summary said.
While supporting all necessary unity within the EU, Kwasniewski will urge the union's current Inter-Governmental Conference to ensure a generally-accepted level of elasticity in European structures.
He is also set to urge the Warsaw government to make an extra effort to strengthen Poland's economy and make the adjustments needed to prepare for EU membership.

Poland hopes to join the EU by the year 2000 and French President Jacques Chirac, during a visit to Warsaw in September, supported this early target although European Commission officials have put 2002 as the earliest realistic date.

Polish officials say the country is now able to meet two of the economic convergence criteria of the Maastricht Treaty which set the framework for currency union -- caps on the budget deficit and on public debt.
Although inflation remains high, they say it can be cut to five percent by 2000.
